name: CivicSense
description: Segregation of waste is important in ensuring sustainable urban environments but manual sorting is inefficient and prone to errors. In this paper, we introduce a comparison benchmark of six deep learning models of waste classification and smart disposal guidance in the form of a system named CivicSense created, which includes a custom Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), MobileNetV3, EfficientNet-B0, ResNet18, DenseNet121, and ConvNeXt-Tiny. The standardized TrashNet waste image datasets were all trained and evaluated with the same preprocessing and augmentation and stratified data splits to compare them fairly. The performance was measured in several dimensions-classification accuracy, macro F1-score, per-class precision and recall, model complexity and inference latency. The experimental findings indicate that the transfer learning architecture is much better than the baseline CNN, and MobileNetV3 and EfficientNet-B0 present the best trade-off between realtime edge deployment and accuracy. Furthermore, UMAP-based visualization of penultimate embeddings also gives an idea of the class separability and learned feature spaces, which proves that CivicSense can be used as a reproducible benchmark in future studies of intelligent waste management. The research complies with SDG 11 and SDG 12 since it will be an advancement of AI-driven solutions to sustainable waste management.
